comments.selected_reason: Plain account of why Miriam was struck.
comments.author: Origen of Alexandria
comments.work: Notes on Numbers

comments.capsule: The spies admitted the land is rich but spoke of a bold nation and walled cities, and so frightened Israel into unmanliness.
comments.comment: Do you understand how the easily terrified and most undaring of those who reconnoitered the land of the promise have confessed evidently that the land is both well-vined and fat, and weighed down with beautiful fruits, yet weave beside these the things unto cowardice, naming the dwelling nation bold, and saying cities fortified and walled up and down, and standing Israel out of the hope unto mastering, and frightening them down unto unmanliness?
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 5

comments.capsule: The spies' report of sons of giants shows they were of great bodies.
comments.comment: But also, when Moses wrote out the spies reporting concerning the hostile land, they said concerning the country: “But we saw sons of giants there” (Numbers 13:33), then interpreting their size they said: “And we were before them as locusts.” Thus it bears witness that they were of great bodies.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind
comments.work: On Genesis

comments.capsule: The glory of the Lord that fills the earth is the Son, who is slain for us like the calf and is himself the sacrifice of salvation.
comments.comment: In truth the glory of the Lord was seen on the eighth day; that is, the Son, the glory of God the Father, became manifest. For God named him so when he said to the most holy Moses, ‘As I live, says the Lord, all the earth shall surely be filled with the glory of the Lord’ (Numbers 14:21). It is he himself who makes us consecrated. He is slain for us, like the calf; he sets us free from sin, releases us from every charge, and scours away the filth that comes from being condemned. He likewise, like the ram, is made perfect for a pleasing spiritual aroma; he himself becomes the sacrifice of salvation and sanctifies us with his own blood (Hebrews 13:12); he himself is the fine flour moistened with oil, in the gladness of a holy life, presenting himself for us to God the Father (Ephesians 5:2).
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 11

comments.capsule: The cowardly and unenduring destroy others with themselves and fall from the hope, while the strong lie inside the hope and are known to God.
comments.comment: Unto this misery and unmanliness every synagogue has slipped down. And although Joshua the of Nun was as it were shifting them unto good daring, and tearing the garment, and pouring countless encomia of the land, they were not wishing to take heart again; yet grieving the helping God with their senseless small-soulednesses, and allotting the success of the hope to their own powers. Therefore thereafter he was also swearing, saying: ‘If any of these men will see the land which I swore to their fathers, except Caleb son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the of Nun.’ (Numbers 14:30) Is it doubtful that the cowardly and unenduring of toil, and short unto faith, destroys others together with himself, corrupting with bad conversations, and will fall from both lot and hope unto God; yet the well-strong and most mighty will both lie inside the hope, and will be known to God?
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 5

comments.capsule: The law adds more fine flour, oil and wine as the animal is larger: a tenth for a lamb, a third for a ram and a half for a calf.
comments.comment: Why, my friend, do you not hear the law saying plainly that if someone chooses to fulfill vows and burnt offerings, and he sacrifices a lamb, he is to add to what is burned a tenth of an ephah of fine flour and a quarter of a hin of wine and of oil? (These, I believe, are Hebrew measures.) But if it is a ram, it says, the accompanying portions come in greater amount, that is, a third; for the measure of a quarter is less than a third. And when a calf is offered, the fine flour and the rest go beyond the third once more, and come at last to a half.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 16

comments.capsule: The loaf of firstfruits shows the bread from heaven that is also from us as one bread, for the Word became like us.
comments.comment: In Numbers, again, he showed us the bread that is from heaven and also from us as one bread, for the Word, though God by nature, became like us and dwelt among us (John 1:14). He showed this when he said to Moses, the revealer of sacred rites: ‘Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: When you go into the land into which I am bringing you, then, when you eat of the bread of the land, you shall take off a portion set apart for the Lord, the firstfruits of your dough. You shall set apart a loaf as an offering; as an offering is taken from the threshing floor, so you shall take off the firstfruits of your dough, and you shall give an offering to the Lord throughout your generations’ (Numbers 15:18–21). Through these words one could see the mystery of the truth without effort.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 9

comments.capsule: The man who gathered dead wood on the Sabbath is a type of those who hold dead works in the season of rest from sins and so bring punishment on themselves.
comments.comment:
But the matter was unto a type of the rest in Christ, and of the ceasing from sin of the one being justified by the faith. Therefore God commanded that the one collecting woods on Sabbath must have died stone-struck; and the justice upon that one was an under-type of an intelligible and necessary matter. Or is not the wood having already been withered from its own root, having been thoroughly cleaned and dried, a symbol of deadness? And would it also otherwise be nurture of fire?

Palladius: Truly.

Cyril: Some such thing is the all-toiling sin, as it were some deadness, and an unholy nurturer of the untamed flame for those loving it. Whenever then as in a season of cessation—I mean the one from sins—some should hold dead and fruitless works, and should choose to love, having let go virtue, the things through which penalties and flames would be kindled for them unto an age, they will reasonably undergo the condemnation upon death, because although it is possible not to live loosely, they willingly go through unto needing to be punished.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 7

comments.capsule: The commandments are marked on doorposts, fastened to the hand and hung from garments, as a remedy for forgetfulness, a hard sickness of mind.
comments.comment: Having commanded beforehand then very well that we write the law down in hearts, then knowing forgetfulness a hard sickness of mind, he commands that the commandments must be marked off as on a tablet upon the doorposts; and indeed also to fasten to the right hand little tablets somehow perhaps pregnant with the law and having the oracle written in, and indeed also that they be hung from the garments themselves, he says is not unprofitable unto benefit—through both fringes and the hyacinth-colored cord.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 7

comments.capsule: The Levites were honored with services under Aaron, and to aim higher than what God had allotted brought punishment and ruin.
comments.comment: With services such as these, then, the whole body of the Levites was honored; and the limit set to their sacred service was to be subject to the one who held first place and to act under the hand of Aaron. But to aim higher than this, and to seek something better than what had been allotted to it and fixed by God, was shown by the event itself to bring punishment and ruin.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 13

comments.capsule: The Kohathites despised the measure allotted to them and treated the high priest's honor as common, which is to find fault with God's decrees.
comments.comment: For the Kohathites, whose service was to carry the most holy things on their shoulders (Numbers 4:4–15), leapt in their ignorance at what lay above them and contended for the rank of the priests. For they seized honors for themselves, as it is written (Hebrews 5:4); they disregarded the divine command; they impiously overran the laws of the priestly service; and they counted the honors of those set over them as worth very little. For they said to Moses and Aaron: ‘Enough from you! For the whole congregation, all of them, are holy, and the Lord is among them.’ (Numbers 16:3) Do you hear how they despise the measure allotted to them, and all but say that the high priest’s honor is common, not to their own clans only but to all the rest as well, and that there is nothing at all exceptional or more distinguished about it, even if those who received the office by God’s own vote are said to stand above them? This is plainly to find fault with the decrees from above and to count the Lawgiver’s decision as nothing.
comments.selected_reason: Explains what was wrong in Korah's words.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 13

comments.capsule: Moses appealed gently to the sons of Levi that it was no small thing to be chosen out of all for so holy a service.
comments.comment: Yet the inspired Moses, with his usual gentleness, appealed to them as to men who were sick; and, having perceived the wrath that was about to fall on them, he rebuked them, saying: ‘Let this be enough for you, sons of Levi. For it is no small thing for you,’ he says, ‘that the God of all has chosen you out of all for a service so holy and so worthy of wonder.’ (Numbers 16:7, 9)
comments.selected_reason: Explains Moses' answer to Korah.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 13

comments.capsule: Korah, Dathan and Abiram, though entrusted with a ministry, thirsted for the glory of Moses and Aaron and seized an honor God had not given them.
comments.comment: Korah, then, and Abiram too, and Dathan besides, sprang from the tribe and blood of Levi. Though they had been entrusted, Scripture says, with a ministry in the holy tent appointed by decree from above, they thirsted for the glory of Moses and Aaron, seizing the honour for themselves, although God had not called them to it (Numbers 16:8–11; Hebrews 5:4). What is more, swelling with savage insolence and exceedingly proud, they poured out on them both abuse that could no longer be borne and was utterly intolerable. Like bulls that scorn the herd they broke away, and shaking off their service under God, they persuaded others to break loose with them into impiety. But they paid the penalty for what they had dared. For the earth opened its mouth and sent that arrogant people down to Hades, with their own kin, their tents and their goods (Numbers 16:31–33).
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 10

comments.capsule: Korah's company seized an honor not assigned to them, which sketched the madness the Jews would later show against Christ, our High Priest.
comments.comment: [Korah and his company,] rising up against the divine laws, brought firepans uninvited, going to this of their own accord and seizing an honor not assigned to them; and out of madness and audacity they drew up their ranks with great heat against the priest who stood first and had been chosen out from all the others (Numbers 16:1–18). Through these events the madness that the Jews would later show against Christ was sketched in outline. For he himself is our High Priest, brought to this by the decision of the Father. Those men paid the penalty for such shameful attempts, and after them the Jews too will pay it, since they have become liable to the same charges.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 9

comments.capsule: Their arrogance ended when the earth opened its mouth and they went down alive into Hades.
comments.comment: But they were still bitter and unyielding, and unbridled in their arrogance, until their madness brought them to such a pitch of evil that the earth opened its mouth, seized them together with their families and their tents, and wrapped them in a strange destruction (Numbers 16:32). For they went down alive into Hades, as it is written (Numbers 16:33).
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 13

comments.capsule: No one should go of his own accord into serving God as a priest, for he who seizes what he is not given will suffer the punishment of Dathan and Abiram.
comments.comment: So the chosen men were called by name to the sacred ministry. For ‘no one takes the honor for himself, but the one who is called by God’ (Hebrews 5:4), as it is written. Let no one, then, go of his own accord into serving God as a priest; let him wait for a call. Otherwise, if he tries to seize what he does not hold by decree from above, he will suffer the punishment of Dathan and Abiram (Numbers 16:31–33).
comments.selected_reason: Explains why Dathan and Abiram were punished.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 11

comments.capsule: The altar was made from the firepans of the rebels as a memorial of the revolt against the great priest, Aaron, a type of Christ.
comments.comment: Then God said to holy Moses, and also to Eleazar the priest, the son of Aaron: ‘Take up the bronze firepans from among those who were burned, and scatter this strange fire there, for the firepans of these sinners have become holy at the cost of their lives. And they made them into hammered plates as a covering for the altar, because they had been offered before the Lord and were made holy. And they became a sign to the sons of Israel.’ (Numbers 16:37–38) This is what God said at that time. And in Exodus it is written about Bezalel, whose father was Uri and whose tribe was Dan, and who led in every kind of skilled craft: ‘He made the bronze altar from the bronze firepans that belonged to the men who rebelled with the company of Korah’ (Exodus 38:22, Septuagint). … But the altar of the worship under the law is shown, mystically and by God’s design, to be a kind of memorial and proclamation in advance, lying in its very construction, of the provocation and defiance, and, if I may now put it so, the revolt, that arose against the great priest. Is the riddle clear to you? For Aaron stands as a type of Christ; and the Jews too contended against the glory of Christ, and for this reason the altar under the law is spoken against.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 9

comments.capsule: The blossoming of the rod showed that Aaron was chosen, and Christ's springing up again from death proves that he is God by nature.
comments.comment: So the blossoming of the rod was no obscure sign that the inspired Aaron, as one of the blood of Levi, had been chosen with distinction and set apart for the priestly service. But when the account is turned once more to spiritual contemplation, the mystery of Christ will shine out again, though still, as it were, in very coarse types. … Emmanuel has been appointed for us by God the Father as Lawgiver and High Priest at once, to offer himself for us as the sacrifice. For as blessed Paul said: ‘The law through Moses appoints as high priests men who have weakness; but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints a Son made perfect for ever’ (Hebrews 7:28). So the Word came down from heaven and became one of us, ‘a minister of the sanctuary and of the true tent, which the Lord pitched, and not man’ (Hebrews 8:2). But those of the blood of Israel did not see fit to think rightly. Setting their own will against him, as it were, they shot at him in many ways with the arrows of envy, no longer holding back their tongues, their insolence or their outrageous schemes; and the wretches, destroying themselves, at last crucified him. Yet the rod from the root of Jesse (Isaiah 11:1) blossomed again. For Christ sprang up again and came back to life, ‘having loosed the pangs of death’ (Acts 2:24), as it is written. Since he is Life by nature, as God, how could he be held by death (Acts 2:24), and not rather triumph over corruption? Just as the springing up of the rod, when wood already past flowering unexpectedly sprouted again, was a sufficient sign to the people of old that Aaron had been appointed high priest by decree from above, so we say that his trampling on death and coming back to life as befits God is a clear, plain and fully sufficient proof that Emmanuel is also God by nature.
comments.selected_reason: Explains what the budding rod signified.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 10

comments.capsule: The priestly rod was said to be of almond wood because the almond is lasting, and the priesthood appeared from Moses until the visitation of the Savior.
comments.comment: Those who have spoken about the nature of plants say this about the “almond”: before all plants in spring it puts forth leaves and casts them off after the casting-off of all the other trees; it is lasting, then. For this reason the priestly “rod” was said to be of “almond-wood” (Numbers 17:8). For it did not remain for a few days: from Moses until the visitation of the Savior it appeared.
comments.selected_reason: Explains why the rod was of almond wood.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind
comments.work: Commentary on Ecclesiastes

comments.capsule: The almond rod is a symbol of sleeplessness, and Christ's return from the dead was an awakening as if from sleep.
comments.comment: In the first place, Palladius, there is nothing unlikely in supposing that the rod was cut from an almond tree; it was the custom among the people of old to use staffs of this kind as well. But if we must also fit to it an explanation suited to spiritual contemplation, I would mention in turn something that is widely repeated, and that seems to some people worth believing: that a rod of almond wood is not without power to cause sleeplessness if it is laid near a person’s head, perhaps producing this effect through natural powers, by the will of God. And he who knows all things, the Maker of the universe, will in some way confirm this for us himself when he says to Jeremiah: ‘What do you see, Jeremiah?’ And Jeremiah said, ‘A staff of almond wood.’ To this God says: ‘You have seen rightly, for I am keeping watch over my words, to perform them’ (Jeremiah 1:11–12). The almond rod, then, would fittingly be understood as a symbol of sleeplessness. And Christ’s return to life from the dead was an awakening, as if from sleep. That is why he also says through the lyre of the Psalmist: ‘I lay down and slept; I awoke, for the Lord upheld me’ (Psalm 3:5).
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 10

comments.capsule: The rising of Christ from death is the sign given to the sons of the disobedient that he is high priest by the vote of the Father.
comments.comment: So the sign that the Son is God by nature and was begotten of God the Father, a sign truly renowned and plain to all and enough to bring the truly fair-minded to faith, is this: he abolished death and corruption and blossomed again into life. ‘For he has become the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep’ (1 Corinthians 15:20) ‘and the firstborn from the dead’ (Colossians 1:18). And the sign has been given to the sons of the disobedient (Numbers 17:10), so that they may know that Christ has become high priest over us by the vote of God the Father, ‘holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and made higher than the heavens’ (Hebrews 7:26), as it is written.
comments.selected_reason: Explains why the rod was kept as a sign for the disobedient.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 10

comments.capsule: The victims offered for sin bear the name sin, which is why Paul applied the law's word to Christ, and what remains of every sacrifice is eaten only in a holy place by males.
comments.comment: From this too, then, you see quite clearly, I think, that he has plainly assigned every kind of sacrifice and offering to the sacred and chosen race, including what comes ‘from every trespass and from all the sins’, that is, the victims offered for every trespass and sin. For the victims offered for sin bear the name ‘sin’. That is why our wise Paul also applied the law’s word to Christ, saying: ‘We beseech you on behalf of Christ, be reconciled to God; for him who knew no sin he made sin for us’ (2 Corinthians 5:20–21). For the Son was sacrificed for our sins according to the Scriptures (1 Corinthians 15:3), as an innocent lamb (Jeremiah 11:19). That the law gave the name ‘sin’ to the victims offered for our sin, God will make clear when he says through the prophet concerning the priests: ‘They shall eat the sins of my people’ (Hosea 4:8); that is, what is offered for the sins of my people shall be food for the priests. So he assigns to them what remains of every sacrifice, and commands that it be eaten, but only in a holy place, he says, and by every male (Numbers 18:10; Leviticus 7:6).
comments.selected_reason: Explains why the sin offerings are called sins and eaten in a holy place.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 12

comments.capsule: The offerings for sin are types of Christ and may be eaten only by the chosen and pure, who are a royal priesthood.
comments.comment: Again, he gives the name ‘sins’ to the victims slain for sins. These too would be types of Christ, who was sacrificed for us and endured the slaughter in order to abolish the sin of the world (John 1:29). And the offerings for sin may be eaten only by those who perform the sacred rites (Leviticus 6:26, 29). For it is fitting that the holy body of Christ be shared not by unholy souls but by chosen and pure ones, to whom one might apply the words, ‘But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for his own possession’ (1 Peter 2:9).
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 13

comments.capsule: The firstfruits and redemption payments, unlike the remains of the sacrifices, may be eaten in the priest's house by his whole household, if the person is clean.
comments.comment: But the firstfruits of oil, grain and wine, the payments for redeeming the firstborn, and the devoted things as well, are to be eaten no longer by the males alone, nor in the holy court, but now in the priest’s house; they are set there for the enjoyment even of his daughters, and of everyone close to him and of his own household. This distinction must be carefully observed. For the remains of the sacrifices would be fitting for the use of the consecrated alone, and will not be common food; and a holy place is the place that befits them. But whatever else is left over, having been brought as a gift, holds, one might say, a second rank of its own once the priest has received it; and it will belong to the priests’ whole household, if only the person is clean, that is, not profane: according to the law, if he is not uncircumcised, not a foreigner, not a leper, not one with a discharge (Leviticus 22:4, 10); but according to the aim of the new Scripture and the Church’s safeguard, if he is not unholy and unbelieving, if he is devout and loves God.
comments.selected_reason: Explains plainly who may eat the firstfruits and gifts, and where.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 12

comments.capsule: Those who wish to serve God without distraction must withdraw from earthly things and make him alone their lot, as the Savior told the man who asked what he still lacked.
comments.comment: [The Lord himself is the Levites’ portion and inheritance.] So too the Savior: when someone once came to him and asked how he might have eternal life (Matthew 19:16), he said, ‘You know the commandments: You shall not murder, You shall not commit adultery, You shall not steal’ (Matthew 19:18; Mark 10:19), and the rest of that kind. The man declared openly that he had kept such commandments, and he asked further, adding, ‘What do I still lack?’ (Matthew 19:20). The Savior answered, ‘If you wish to be perfect, go, sell your possessions and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me’ (Matthew 19:21). Those, then, who wish to serve God without distraction, and who think they must follow him, have to withdraw from earthly things, make him alone their lot, and grow rich on their hope in him, as is sung in the Psalms: ‘Delight in the Lord, and hope in him, and he will act’ (Psalm 37:4–5).
comments.selected_reason: Explains what it means that the Lord is the Levites' portion.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 13

comments.capsule: The sacred race is marked off from the people by the difference of its hope: the earthbound are given their portion, but those chosen for virtue have the Lord as their inheritance.
comments.comment: See, then, how the sacred race is not ranked with the people, and is in a way marked off from the rest, not only by the duties of its ministry but already by the difference of its hope. For to those who live an earthbound life, who cling to earthly things and thirst for the things of the moment, which pass by like shadows, it may fittingly be said: ‘This is your portion, this is your lot, the portion for your disobedience to me, says the Lord.’ (Jeremiah 13:25) But to those who have prized the holy and blameless life, and who are already chosen out for their virtue, it is very right to say: ‘You shall have no inheritance in their land, and you shall have no portion among them; for I am your portion and your inheritance… (Numbers 18:20)
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 13

comments.capsule: The Levites receive the tithes as pay, for the saints' toil is not unpaid.
comments.comment: So he sets apart the tithes for the Levites, in return for the labor of their service (Numbers 18:21). For the toil of the saints is not unpaid: their honors are choice and their rewards splendid.
comments.selected_reason: Explains why the Levites receive the tithes.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 13

comments.capsule: The priests received tithes as their portion and gave a tenth to Aaron, who is a type of Christ ministering in the inner and hidden tabernacle.
comments.comment: “Take away from it an offering” (Numbers 18:26). Those who were called to serve as priests according to the law of Moses received tithes from the sons of Israel as their portion and inheritance from God. They in turn offered a tenth to the one who presided over and led the priesthood, that is, to Aaron. He has also been set as a type of Christ, ministering not in the first tabernacle, the one that has its visible structure, but in the inner and hidden one.
comments.selected_reason: Explains the priests' tithe of the tithe and what Aaron points to.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: Fragments on Numbers

comments.capsule: Aaron signifies Christ, the Priest of priests, and the one who receives tithes has himself been tithed.
comments.comment: Do you see the mystery of Christ, still in shadows, as it were, and shining out beforehand in types? For the one who receives tithes has himself been tithed, as the blessed Paul says (Hebrews 7:9). But at that time the type was in Melchizedek (Genesis 14:18–20); in the times of Moses it was kept again, as it were, in Aaron, who signifies in himself Christ, the Priest of priests, who leads and presides over the holy tent, that is, the Church: the Holy of holies and the God of gods, to whom we owe all the fruit we bear. For it is written: ‘All who are round about him shall bring gifts’ (Psalm 76:11). But the things of Moses are still in types, while now the true guardians of the Gospel’s commands gladden their Redeemer with spiritual fruit.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 13

comments.capsule: Under the law touching a corpse made one unclean, but now the one who touches the bones of a martyr receives a share of sanctification.
comments.comment: When they died in the Jewish manner, the corpses were abominable. When death is for Christ's sake, the remains of his holy ones are precious. Before this, it was said to the priests and the Nazirites: “You shall not be defiled by any dead person,” and, “If anyone touches a corpse, he shall be unclean until evening,” and, “He shall wash his garments” (Leviticus 21:1; Numbers 19:11, 19). But now the one who touches the bones of a martyr receives a certain share of sanctification from the grace that attends the body.
comments.selected_reason: Explains how the uncleanness of the dead is changed for those who die for Christ.
comments.author: Basil of Caesarea
comments.work: Homily on Psalm 115

comments.capsule: The law counted touching a dead body as defilement to show that deadness is hateful to God, who gives life, and as a type of the deadness of the mind that loves sin.
comments.comment: Now as for some being unclean through the dead, this means something like the following. To touch one who has departed and to come near a dead body the law counted, for the people of old, as a kind of defilement (Numbers 19:11), showing that deadness is hateful to God, who has power to give life to all things. It also took the matter in another way, as a rough type of the deadness of mind and soul. And the mind that loves sin, and is used to having no share in the noble deeds that lead to life, is dead and cold. But if someone happened to die, it was altogether necessary that his relatives by blood and family should gather and perform the customary rites over him; yet these too were unclean according to the law, though not for good and for all time, for there was a way for them to be cleansed (Numbers 19:12). There you have a sufficient explanation of the literal history.
comments.selected_reason: Explains why contact with the dead made a person unclean.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 14

comments.capsule: The heifer's ashes mixed with water point to the dying of Jesus accomplished in baptism, which is to die to the world and to sins and live the life that is in him.
comments.comment: [The dying of Christ is this:] To have died to the world and to sins, and to live out a life that is sacred and holy and as dear to God as possible. Paul again took great pride in this, when he said: ‘For through the law I died to the law, so that I might live to God. I have been crucified with Christ; it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me. And the life I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me’ (Galatians 2:19–20). This, I think, is what it means to have died to the world and to have undergone the dying of Christ, and in turn to live out the life that is in him. So the heifer’s ashes mixed with water (Numbers 19:17) would point to the dying of Jesus as it is accomplished in holy baptism. And he said that even those who served in the Levitical order must share in it, once they had cast off, again as in a shadow, every kind of uncleanness of the flesh.
comments.selected_reason: Explains what the ashes mixed with water signify.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 11

comments.capsule: The ash with water stands for the Savior's passion, which ransoms from sin and washes the defilements of our souls.
comments.comment: And for those who have been defiled, the cleansing is the ash with water (Numbers 19:17). For the Savior’s passion is the ransom from sin; he sanctifies us through water, through which we gain not the removal of the filth of the flesh, as it is written (1 Peter 3:21), but the washing away of the defilements in our souls. For ‘Wash yourselves,’ it says, ‘and become clean’ (Isaiah 1:16): so a prophetic word commanded us long ago.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 15

comments.capsule: God confirms their faith by recalling the wonders in Egypt, and Christ is compared to a rock for its unshakable nature.
comments.comment: “Take the rod and assemble the congregation” (Numbers 20:8). Observe that, God confirms their faith by directing them to remember the wonders worked in Egypt by saying, “Take the rod in your hand, with which you struck the river” (Exodus 7:20, LXX). … Christ is compared to a rock because of its unbreakable and unshakable nature.
comments.selected_reason: Explains why the rod is named and what the rock is compared to.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: Fragments on Numbers

comments.capsule: Edom, though kin to Israel, refused them passage and marched out against them, and the heretics, with their false show of brotherhood, are like this toward those who walk uprightly.
comments.comment: The Ammonites, being descended from Esau, were near kin and of one blood with the sons of Jacob, I mean Israel. Yet those from Esau somehow disregarded nature itself and were false to the bond of kinship; from then on they proved harsh and unbending toward those who were close to them and of their own blood, that is, toward Israel. For when Israel set out from the land of the Egyptians and was passing by the country of the Ammonites, he begged the man who lived there, as a brother, to let them pass or hurry through, and to pity them as people who had been wronged; but he would not give way. But why do I say this? He went further: he took up arms and even made war. And he would have done them terrible harm had Israel not turned aside at the word of God. … Do you not see that, though they were joined to Israel by the tie of kinship, they were shown by the events themselves to be without natural affection and hard of heart, no different from wild beasts? When they ought to have pitied them as brothers, toiling and sweating as they were, they marched out to lay them waste. That is why the law says: ‘They shall not enter the assembly of the Lord, because they did not meet you with bread and water when you were coming out of Egypt’ (Deuteronomy 23:3–4); that is, because they were so utterly without compassion and had strayed into the unholiness of savage ways. You can see that the heretics, both their peoples and their leaders, are like this toward us who have chosen to walk uprightly. For as far as knowing the one and only God, the Father, and accepting faith in the Son and the Spirit is concerned, though not wholly soundly, they have a false show of brotherhood with us, and their kinship is counterfeit in intent.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 14

comments.capsule: Aaron's going to the fathers is release from the body, as the righteous man comes out of the house of prisoners to reign.
comments.comment: He goes away to the fathers. Which fathers? About whom Paul says: For this reason I bend my knees to the Father, from whom every family. Thus according to us Aaron was released. For it is also written in Ecclesiastes about the righteous man who has contested well, who has gone out from the bodily bond, that He shall come out of the house of prisoners to reign.
comments.author: Origen of Alexandria
comments.work: Dialogue with Heraclides

comments.capsule: Aaron goes up the mountain to die and Eleazar to take up the priesthood, and the mountain signifies what stands out in glory.
comments.comment: Do you understand, then, how they are brought up: Aaron to die and come to his end, and the one born of him, that is, Eleazar, to take up the priesthood? The mountain would signify what is visible from every side and set on high, what stands out in glory. So let it be said from now on to everyone who is brought to priestly service: ‘A city set on a mountain cannot be hidden.’ (Matthew 5:14)
comments.selected_reason: Explains what Aaron's death on the mountain and Eleazar's succession signify.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 13

comments.capsule: The one who looks to the bronze serpent lives, as the one who understands the mystery of the Word who became as we are conquers death.
comments.comment: The serpents were biting those of Israel in the desert; then the God of all commanded Moses to set up a bronze serpent: “And it shall be,” he says, “if a serpent bites a human, and he looks toward the serpent, he shall also live.” (Numbers 21:8–9) What then is the riddle? And why is the one who looks at the serpent saved? Therefore the Only-begotten Word of God, existing as life by nature, became in the likeness that is as we are—that is, human (Romans 8:3); and the human is evil and as it were the serpent; yet even if he became as we are, if someone looks to him, he conquers death. And what is it to look to him, except precisely to understand carefully the mystery upon him? For then one will see him in the likeness of the evil ones—that is, of humans—yet life-giving as God, and making the bites of the evil serpents vanish. So there is one Lord and Son, the same one, both life-giving as God and in the form of the evil ones through economy.
comments.selected_reason: Explains why looking at the bronze serpent saves.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On the True Faith, to the Princesses Arcadia and Marina

comments.capsule: The serpent hung on wood signifies the passion of the Savior hung on wood.
comments.comment: For the Savior himself says: "As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of man be lifted up," (John 3:14) according to the type of the serpent hung on the wood by Moses, signifying nothing other than the passion of the Savior insofar as he was hung on wood. It is clear, then, that the passion will be taken according to the type of the serpent and not according to the type of the Passover
comments.author: Origen of Alexandria
comments.work: On Pascha

comments.capsule: The Moabites hired Balaam to curse Israel, but by God's power the soothsayer's mouth was turned to blessings they did not want.
comments.comment: Now consider the Moabites too, if you like, who were openly the bitterest enemies of those who wish to serve the God who alone is God by nature and in truth. They were worshippers of idols, who put special trust in divinations and sorceries and were taken up beyond all measure with the flights of birds. Grinding their teeth at Israel’s good fortune, they hired Balaam and set him to curse; but by the inexpressible power of God the soothsayer’s mouth was turned to blessings they did not want (Numbers 22:5–6; Deuteronomy 23:4–5). Such would be the war that the pagans wage against us. They begrudge our Savior his glory and stir up all the strength of the devil against us; but divine grace from above shakes that strength down, pours feebleness over the herd of demons, and turns their way of plotting into something that brings gladness.
comments.selected_reason: Explains how Balak's plan to curse Israel failed.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 14

comments.capsule: God turned Balaam away from cursing so that Israel would never become catchable by Moabites or Midianites, God shielding the people clinging to him.
comments.comment: And seeking cold and demonic dreamlets, and expecting things happening for him perhaps from a charm and also sorcery, he said the Lord would speak to him; for he was pretending to call-upon-God. Yet even if the sacred Letter uses the customary voices of the sorcerers, we would not think, thinking rightly, that God who is by nature and truly sends the true as from love into profane souls, and talks toward a foul man and sorcerer and idolater. Yet, ‘God came,’ it says, ‘toward Balaam, and said to him: What are these humans beside you?’ (Numbers 22:9) And when that one had announced the cause of the arrival, ‘God said,’ it says, ‘toward Balaam: You will not go with them, nor will you curse the people; for it is blessed.’ Behold clearly from God’s person the blessed angel turns away the deceiver and empty-speaker sorcerer from seeking to curse the one blessed beside God, and from setting opposite the votes from above the inventions from human ill-counsel—not as if the curse were strong to wrong, but in order that the one who has unreasonably received such a hope might be clearly and evidently informed, and through him, that Israel would never become catchable for Moabites or Midianites, God shielding and contending, and walling with favors the people clinging to him and having been blessed.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 6

comments.capsule: The angel allowed Balaam to go but stood in the road with a flashing sword, teaching that his war would be against God and angels if he cursed the blessed ones.
comments.comment: Yet these things the divine angel both said and was commanding to do; and when the diviner was baited by the promises of gifts unto needing to walk, having perhaps also truly supposed he would be strong, the blessed angel allows to go, yet was seen in the middle of the road, with a flashing sword, teaching clearly that the war for him is toward both God and angels, if he should wish to curse the blessed ones.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 6

comments.capsule: Balaam prayed in a divine spirit to die to sin in order to live to God.
comments.comment: But according to the remaining significations, according to the one the soul is mortal, and blessed if it dies to sin. About this death Balaam, prophesying, spoke, praying in a divine spirit: May my soul die in the souls of the righteous. About this death Balaam prophesied in a strange way, and he prayed the finest things for himself in the word of God. For he prayed to die to sin in order to live to God. And for this reason he said: May my soul die in the souls of the righteous, and may my seed be as the seed of these.
comments.selected_reason: Explains what Balaam meant by asking that his soul die the death of the righteous.
comments.author: Origen of Alexandria
comments.work: Dialogue with Heraclides

comments.capsule: For the one who always follows Jesus there is no toil, since the following itself takes away the labor.
comments.comment: If then you become such that you always follow Jesus, you will also follow, and as long as you follow you will not grow weary; for 'there will be no toil in Jacob, nor will pain be seen in Israel.' (Numbers 23:21) There is no labor for the one following Jesus; the very following takes away the labor.
comments.selected_reason: Explains what it means that there is no toil in Jacob.
comments.author: Origen of Alexandria
comments.work: Homilies on Jeremiah

comments.capsule: God turned people from augury by causing a spirit in the augur to say there is no augury in Jacob.
comments.comment: And once, when God wished to turn people away from augury through an augur, He caused a spirit in the augur to say: “For there is no augury in Jacob, nor divination in Israel; in due time it will be told to Jacob and to Israel what God will accomplish” (Numbers 23:23).
comments.selected_reason: Explains why Balaam says there is no augury in Jacob.
comments.author: Origen of Alexandria
comments.work: Against Celsus, Book IV

comments.capsule: Those who have Jesus Christ as Lord will rule over many dominions.
comments.comment: And he will rule over many nations (Numbers 24:7). There are indeed many lords and many gods, but blessed are those who have our Lord Jesus Christ as Lord, for they will rule over many dominions.
comments.selected_reason: Plain explanation of the rule over many nations.
comments.author: Origen of Alexandria
comments.work: Notes on Numbers

comments.capsule: By a divine power Balaam was turned from cursing to blessing Israel, to Balak's grief.
comments.comment: at once he [Balaam] was a prophet, not the customary and false-speaker, but by a divine and unspeakable power he was turned contrary to hope toward the opposite. For he was cursing not at all, yet was rather blessing Israel, and sends bitter griefs into Balak.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 6

comments.capsule: Balaam's disciples kept his prophecy of a rising star, and the Magi received it by ancestral tradition and came to Bethlehem.
comments.comment: And a man from Israel shall rise (Numbers 24:17). They say that Balaam had disciples in his art, men who had been instructed by him in magic, and that they held an opinion about him and wrote down his prophecies and left them behind, including the one that says, "A star shall rise." It was through receiving this from ancestral tradition and succession that the Magi came to Bethlehem.
comments.selected_reason: Explains how the Magi came to know the prophecy of the star.
comments.author: Origen of Alexandria
comments.work: Notes on Numbers

comments.capsule: False persons' words are not to be allegorized unless God acted through them, as in Balaam.
comments.comment: Do not allegorize the words of false persons, nor seek anything spiritual in them, unless God has acted through economy, as in Balaam (Numbers 24:17) and Caiaphas (John 11:50-51), so that one speaks concerning the birth and the other concerning the death of our Savior.
comments.author: Evagrius Ponticus
comments.work: The Gnostic

comments.capsule: No prophecy is recorded about comets, but Balaam prophesied the star that rose at the birth of Jesus.
comments.comment: But I would say that no prophecy is on record about comets, to the effect that such and such a comet will rise in such a reign or at such times. About the star that rose at the birth of Jesus, however, Balaam prophesied, as Moses recorded, saying: “A star will rise out of Jacob, and a man will rise up out of Israel” (Numbers 24:17).
comments.selected_reason: Explains how the star of the Magi was foretold.
comments.author: Origen of Alexandria
comments.work: Against Celsus, Book I

comments.capsule: The magi, skilled in Balaam's arts, had his prophecies about the star and guessed that the man foretold with it had come.
comments.comment: It seems to me, then, that they had the prophecies of Balaam, which Moses also recorded, since Balaam himself had been skilled in such arts. There they found what is said about the star, and the words, “I will show him, but not now; I call him blessed, but he will not draw near” (Numbers 24:17). From this they guessed that the man foretold together with the star had come into the world; and having concluded beforehand that he was stronger than all the demons and than the beings that usually appeared to them and worked for them, they wished “to worship” him (Matthew 2:2).
comments.author: Origen of Alexandria
comments.work: Against Celsus, Book I

comments.capsule: Those baptized in the cloud and the sea, though they had eaten the bread from heaven, were carried into apostasy because they shared meals with the idolaters.
comments.comment: And what happened to the people of old after this? In what way did they stumble? They were defiled at Shittim, they served idols, they were initiated into the rites of Baal of Peor (Numbers 25:1–3; Psalm 106:28). See, then, how those baptized in the cloud and in the sea, though they had eaten the bread from heaven and drunk the spiritual drink, became entangled with the idolaters. Because they shared meals with them and touched the table of the idols, they were at once easily carried away and slid into apostasy, and they danced with women: “And the people who understood were entangled with a prostitute,” in the words of the prophet (Hosea 4:14). For this is what is meant by “they rose up to play” (1 Corinthians 10:7).
comments.selected_reason: Explains how Israel fell into idolatry at Shittim.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: Fragments on 1 Corinthians

comments.capsule: The Moabites let down adorned women to draw Israel from the worship of God, and strengthened apostasy together with the fornication.
comments.comment: And knowing that the male is hot and easy toward the female, and that youth is not secure with the most foul pleasures unto this, they were letting down women adorned, unto conversation not decent for those from Israel, by whose beauties everything as much as was easy toward being sick with the things of flesh was most ready snatched together, and was being carried aside little by little from the worship unto God, following those women’s judgments. And they were strengthening apostasy together with the fornication.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 4

comments.capsule: Israel worshiped the idols but did not serve them, for it is not said that they served them.
comments.comment: So too the profaned people worshiped but served not idols, 'unto the daughters of Moab.' For it stands written in these very words that they called them to the sacrifices of their idols, and the people ate of their sacrifices, 'and worshiped their idols, and were joined to Belphegor.' (Numbers 25:1–3) And observe that it is not said 'and served their idols' — for it was not possible, under one season's moment, with such signs and wonders, to be persuaded by the women with whom they fornicated to deem the idols gods.
comments.selected_reason: Explains the wording that the people worshiped but did not serve the idols.
comments.author: Origen of Alexandria
comments.work: Exhortation to Martyrdom

comments.capsule: Unbridled pleasure led Israel to give up piety, so they were made an example in the face of the sun, a type that no one caught in such sins escapes the all-seeing Judge.
comments.comment: Do you see how the divine and most gentle nature is somehow provoked by us, and all but driven into an anger it does not desire? For it is a thing fit for beasts, I mean going mad over the beauty of women; and it is utterly unholy as well to dare to give up piety toward God in exchange for unbridled pleasure. That is why they are made an example before the Lord in the face of the sun: that is, they were hung on upright stakes turned toward the east, and this was the manner of their punishment. The type all but cries out plainly and raises its voice to say that no one caught in such sins will escape the all-seeing eye of the Judge, which cannot be deceived, nor will he get away unpunished; rather, as the prophet’s word says, he will be set out ‘as a spectacle to all flesh’ (Isaiah 66:24), paying the bitter penalty for his offenses.
comments.selected_reason: Explains why the guilty were made an example in the face of the sun.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 14

comments.capsule: The fornicators suffered unbearable disasters, consumed by the hand of brother and neighbor.
comments.comment: The lawgiver therefore was indignant upon these things also most reasonably, and the matter was not without penalty for those from Israel. For they were at once in unbearable disasters through this, the fornicators being consumed by brother’s and neighbor’s hand.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 4

comments.capsule: God orders that those who have come to full stature be numbered, since those ready to act against passions and sin are written in his book and inherit the holy land.
comments.comment: Gathering the mind therefore in few of what lies before, we say that: God orders that what has come to puberty again, and the war-experienced stature, must be numbered up. For as we already said having arrived, in knowledge and enrollment beside God, and in a book of living, not the strengthless and inactive, nor indeed what still infants according to thinking, but every thing as much as is already well-strong and ready unto array against passions and sin, and stepped unto understanding, and already decent toward the need to act and be able to succeed at whatever God would wish; and these portioned the land very well according to tribes, and from name, and according to each; for heirs of the holy land will be, and will share the goods in hopes
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 4

comments.capsule: God honors each in proportion to his successes, and the larger inheritance for the larger number is a type of increase in virtue, allotted by a divine vote.
comments.comment: Yet also according to one and from name is the crown of good fame, God honoring each proportionally to his own successes, and measuring out the fitting grace for those playing the man, even if it happen to be understood as in a greater measure, and richer distribution; for ‘A good measure,’ (Luke 6:38) he says, ‘pressed, shaken, pouring over they will give into your bosom’ (Luke 6:38); and this very thing I think somewhere the saying of God makes clear: ‘To the more you will increase their inheritance, and to the fewer you will lessen their inheritance; to each, just as they were overseen, their inheritance will be given.’ (Numbers 26:54) For as in a greater number of the names would become a clear type of the overlying and increasing in virtue; for one is approved thus, and another thus, according to blessed Paul. And the land is allotted, according somewhere perhaps to that: ‘In your hands are my lots’; said toward God. For by a divine vote will come to be the unwandering distribution of the goods about to be, the one knowing all things according to us then defining for each what is fitting unto allotment.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 4

comments.capsule: The Levites are numbered apart from a month old and have God as their lot, the knowledge concerning the Godhead seen by the pure in heart.
comments.comment: And again the Levites’ numbering-up is private, from a month old and upward. And a lot is not given them in the middle of the sons of Israel, nor were they overseen together with them. For somewhere the more sacred race is always more holy. Therefore also the enrollment concerning it is excepted from the others, and a lot for them is not with the others, but also a private oversight; and a portion and lot for them is the God of the wholes himself, according to: ‘Blessed are the pure in heart, because they themselves will see God.’ (Matthew 5:8) For of the so-called poor in spirit about to inherit the kingdom of the heavens, and of those choosing to mourn about to be comforted, and of the merciful about to be mercied: The pure in heart, he says, are blessed, because they themselves will see God. And these would be those more sacred and more holy beyond all the others, and a lot and portion for them is the precise God-seeing—that is, the knowledge concerning the Godhead.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 4

comments.capsule: The lamb slain in the first month is a type of Christ, whose death bears much fruit, and the calves, ram and lambs added signify the multitude called through faith.
comments.comment:
Look then, Palladius, at Emmanuel’s death bearing much fruit, according to what he said clearly and truly: ‘Amen, amen, I say to you: unless the grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.’ (Jn 12:24; Num 28:23)

For the lamb is slaughtered as a type of Christ, in the first month according to the law, on the fourteenth day. And calves and a ram and lambs are added for sacrifice and holocausts — signifying, I think, both the multitude of those called through faith into holiness and the measure of spiritual vigor, as in a type. (Ex 12:6)

For if Christ had not died for us, we would not have been received as a fragrance of sweet smell. …
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 17

comments.capsule: What we promise to God we must pay without delay, for the law records delay or failure to pay a vow as sin.
comments.comment: So we must pay to God what we have promised, and whatever anyone vows, let him carry it out without delay. For I would count failing to do such things promptly among the most dreadful and dangerous of faults, and so does sacred Scripture itself. If, thinking rightly, we reckon it among the most outrageous things to be convicted on a charge of lying, how would it not be utterly shameful to pledge something and promise it to God, and afterwards to prove false to that promise? So whenever anyone has vowed and then delayed, or has even shrunk back from paying altogether, the law records it against him as sin (Deuteronomy 23:21).
comments.selected_reason: Explains why a vow must be kept.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 16

comments.capsule: Those who act under another's hand are released from the charge.
comments.comment: But it releases from the charge those who have nothing at all of their own, but are yoked as by a binding necessity and act under another’s hand.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 16

comments.capsule: Anyone free and outside the yoke is liable to blame for not doing what they promised, but those who live under others are rightly released.
comments.comment: And even if, it says, the woman is lawfully married to a husband, the same law is to hold (Numbers 30:6–8). For a widow, however, and for a divorced woman, he lets the pledges stand (Numbers 30:9), and says, very rightly, that the promises must be carried out in every way and by all means. Everywhere he holds anyone who is free and outside the yoke liable to blame, if they will not choose to do what they promised; but anyone not so placed, who has no power to act and lives under others, he rightly releases.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 16

comments.capsule: A father or husband who lets a vow stand is charged if it is not kept, for offerings come from free choice.
comments.comment: [When the father or the husband has agreed] …to the vows of those under their hand and authority, he brings the charge of impiety if they do not choose to fulfill what was promised (Numbers 30:14–15). But when they refuse, he also rules that there must be release from sin; for offerings dedicated to God are the fruits of free choice, not of compulsion.
comments.selected_reason: Explains why the husband bears the guilt of a vow he let stand.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 16

comments.capsule: A thousand chosen from each tribe were brought together so that what is approved in each might become a boast of the whole.
comments.comment: These things God having oracled, chosen young men were being brought together toward the war’s need; and from every tribe was flowing together what is most enduring of hardship and most proven, so that what is approved from each might become a boast of the whole, and the part’s brightness might go unto the whole fullness, according at least to what has been said wisely by Paul: ‘For if one member suffers, all the members suffer together; if one member is glorified, all the members rejoice together.’ (1 Corinthians 12:26)
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 4

comments.capsule: Phinehas the priest, the holy vessels and the trumpets sketch Christ our high priest, the angels, and those who proclaim the divine word.
comments.comment: The most strong multitude of the chosen was therefore campaigning against the Midianites, Phinehas the priest being with them, and the holy vessels, and indeed also trumpets, of the so-called signals. For Christ, our great high priest, is always fellow-armed and fellow-stander for those playing the man; and angels also contend together, being hinted as in the holy vessels. For holy and liturgical vessels are the rational spirits in heaven; for they have been ordered by God toward our help. And the trumpets of the signals are present no less—that is, the words of those who speak God—signaling very well in what manner one must play the man against the enemies, or rather the passions being in us. Therefore a sketch of Christ is the priest—that is, Phinehas; of angels, the holy vessels; and of those who have cried through to us the divine word, the trumpets of the signals. For thus without toil we will prevail over those who have stood against in Christ, saying what is sung in Psalms: ‘In you we will gore our enemies, and in your name we will set at naught those who rise up upon us.’ (Psalm 44:5)
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 4

comments.capsule: Even the best of the chosen are not blameless, so the conquerors were cleansed outside the camp on the third and the seventh day.
comments.comment: You see that even the best and approved race of the chosen in us is not altogether blameless; for ‘No one is clean from filth,’ even if someone should be very much of those accustomed to be approved; for the perfectly holy has been kept unto the age about to be. Outside the camp therefore he seats the conquerors, and says they must be purified on the third day and the seventh. The third day either signaling for us the third time, in which the cleansing through Christ came to be after the time according to Moses, and in which the choir of the holy prophets was shown, or rather that of the resurrection, in which Christ lived again, having nailed to the precious cross the handwriting against us, and having endured the suffering that looses sin for us. And the seventh persuading us to understand the time upon the completion of the present age, in which having shaken off the burden of sin wholly, and going unto an allotment of sanctification, we will be with Christ, wearing a clean and purified life, and in blessedness according to Christ.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 4

comments.capsule: Things passed through fire and water show our cleansing through Christ, who baptizes in Holy Spirit and fire, with the perfect cleansing at the completion of the age.
comments.comment: For he has ordered that as many things as among the vessels were able to pass the fire’s edge be brought through fire; and as many as do not have natural strength, but are somehow rotten and readier unto being able to suffer disappearance altogether—saying clothing, and what is from skins and woods—be carried through water, as enigmatically showing us in golden and silver vessels and in the others, for whom the cleansing through Christ has come to be as in fire and water. For we have been baptized in Holy Spirit and fire. Therefore the being carried through fire and water of the things gathered from the captivity newly hints our cleansing, whom Christ has made his own as some devilish wealth once, having gone into the strong one’s house, and having plundered his vessels, and having bound the strong one. And Eleazar says the conquerors will barely go into the camp then, when they wash the garments on the seventh day, and thus will be clean. For the perfect cleansing, and putting-away of every filth, will be in last times of the completion, just as I said newly, sin being removed altogether, and human nature being carried up unto the from-above and most ancient beauty. For ‘There will be then,’ (Isaiah 35:8) he says, ‘a clean road, and it will be called a holy road. And no unclean one will pass by there, but those redeemed through the Lord will walk in it.’ (Isaiah 35:8)
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 4

comments.capsule: Each conqueror's vessels going through fire and water also show the saints' souls being tested.
comments.comment: Yet if someone should choose that one must understand also otherwise, we say that: he has ordered each conqueror’s vessel, whether it happen to be golden, or silver, or also from bronze, and made from other material, to go through fire; for as blessed Paul writes, ‘The fire will test of what sort each one’s work (1 Corinthians 3:13) is.’ And he has ordered also some things to come through water; for the word of the psalmody hints to us that the saints’ souls are tested not otherwise, except according to some such manners. And indeed David was singing that ‘You tested us, O God; you fired us, as silver is fired; we passed through fire and water, and you led us out unto refreshment.’
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 4

comments.capsule: The chosen thousand shared the spoils of war with the whole congregation, so that the brightness of the part comes to the whole, as one fragrance rises from different incenses.
comments.comment: And we were saying clearly and evidently that the part’s brightness and good reputation will come unto the whole fullness, this also being managed for us very well of God’s gentleness and love of humans, so that as of one and most fragrant incense, made from different forms, some one fragrance of all thereafter may be carried up to God, and what is not thus approved may somehow be made bright together with the very most approved. … Observe then these things unveiled, God legislating them for those from Israel; for the chosen thousand according to tribe were campaigning against the Midianites; and winning, I think somewhere, gaining by toil and sweat, they distributed the things gathered from the war toward every synagogue at once, and the other multitude was being solemnized by the successes of those playing the man; for ‘Divide,’ he says, ‘the spoils, you and Eleazar the priest, and the rulers of the fatherhoods of the synagogue; and divide the spoils in the middle of the warriors going out unto the array, and in the middle of the synagogue.’ (Numbers 31:26–31)
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 4

comments.capsule: Those of lower rank will be perfected together with the chosen, and the small are blessed with the great.
comments.comment: You see how those having the deficient rank will also be perfected together with those in the end, and those not strong according to them are blessed together with the chosen? And the divine David also sings somewhere: ‘Blessed are you by the Lord, who made the heaven and the earth; the Lord has blessed Aaron’s house (Psalm 115:15); the Lord has blessed Israel’s house; the Lord has blessed those who fear him, the small with the great.’ The so-called small are blessed together with the great, not having to boast in equal strength, and being worsted in eagernesses unto the need to endure hardship, yet perhaps being equaled in zeal and faith, and delighting Christ with strengths according to power.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 4

comments.capsule: Moses and Eleazar are a type of Christ, lawgiver and high priest, who will distribute to each the honors fitting him.
comments.comment:
And Moses and Eleazar would be a type of the one high priest and lawgiver Christ, distributing the spoils to the people, holy angels standing by together, of whom also the rulers of the fatherhoods of the synagogue would be a type. Or do you not say that many of the holy angels upon earth have been ordered by God, unto the need to help those who have believed, and as it were to lead peoples?

Palladius: I say so; for how not?

Cyril: Christ is expected to come from heaven with the holy angels, and will sit upon his throne of glory, and will distribute to each the prizes fitting him, and the honors proportionally to the successes; therefore also wise Isaiah says to us concerning Christ: ‘Because of this he himself will lord over many, and of the strong he will divide spoils, instead of things for which his soul was handed over unto death, and was reckoned among the lawless.’ (Isaiah 53:12) In Christ therefore is the distribution of the goods, as typed in Moses and Eleazar. For Christ is lawgiver in the same and high priest.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 4

comments.capsule: The leaders honor God with brighter and more decent offerings, giving even what the law did not require.
comments.comment: You hear how he says an precise reckoning of those who have fought came to be, so that no one remained from whom the gift has not been brought forward, according at least to what seems good to the divine nods? And they themselves say they have also wished to bring forward to the Lord even what he himself has not judged one must bring forward—bracelet and ring, and armlet, and as many things as have been made in golden adornment. For the lawgiver has ordered to make the gifts from the humans and from the beasts; and indeed it has been brought forward according to the divine and heavenly arrangement; yet they make a willing bringing-forward of the exceptional in treasures; and the leaders of the chosen conquer the law’s limit with their ambitions. And indeed Moses and Aaron having taken, have brought them into the holy tent; and making them stored as a memorial before the Lord; for those leading peoples, and set unto rulers, honor God with bright and more decent offerings …
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 4

comments.capsule: Reuben and Gad, for the sake of cattle and love of wives and children, would not have crossed the Jordan and barely promise to go across with the others, like those compressed by the cares of this life.
comments.comment: You understand that for the sake of cattle-feeding and possessions, and of love unto wives and children, such ones would not at all have crossed the Jordan, nor would they have endured even so much as to sharpen for war and battle, nor would they have wished to share good-repute with the others, and the goods upon hopes; yet remaining seemed best and much-wished to them, not even, so to speak, setting the foot into Jordan’s streams; yet Moses reproaching and persuading them to dread, and to look askance at the divine anger, they barely promise that they will go across the Jordan together with the others, and will share with them the sweats in war and battles; yet not that they will also share the portion, they say, because of having or keeping off the lot beyond the Jordan. Some such in manner are those compressed by the cares of the present life.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 5

comments.capsule: Those who have crossed the Jordan must destroy the idols and steles without sparing, for sparing such evils shows a heart not dedicated to God.
comments.comment: You understand that those who have passed the Jordan must make altars and precincts from the midst, and pry up without care the idols themselves and steles? as for allotting sparing perhaps to such evils, it would become a clear indication of not having been fixed well, nor dedicating the heart unaccused to God, although he says clearly concerning the godless and evil: ‘You will not worship their gods, nor will you serve according to their works, but with a taking-down you will take down, and crushing you will crush their steles, and you will serve the Lord your God, and I will bless your bread, and your wine, and your water; and I will turn weakness away from you; there will not be barren, nor sterile upon your land; I will fill up the number of your days.’ (Exodus 23:24) For it is not unclear that for those very well fixed and from a healthy mind clinging to the God of all, and having practiced to make a clear demonstration of the matter—the shaking down of altars and steles, and playthings of humans corrupted in mind—it will be a procurer of divine gifts.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 6

comments.capsule: Levi had no allotment but God, yet was given a little for necessary use so as not to seem wholly set apart.
comments.comment: So he made the tribe of Levi a tribe without an allotment, and gave himself to it as its special lot. Yet he wisely did not let them seem to be set wholly apart from the rest by receiving nothing at all; he measured the matter out, as it were, and gave them a little for their necessary use.
comments.selected_reason: Explains why the Levites receive cities though they have no allotment.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 13

comments.capsule: Particular cities are honors for the holy ministers, but Jerusalem is common to all.
comments.comment: Particular lots, then, and indeed cities set apart from the rest (Numbers 35:2–8), are the honors God gives to the holy ministers; but he appoints, as common, as it were, to all, the one renowned Jerusalem.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 13

comments.capsule: The saints may possess what sustains life, and the Levites were given small towns and fields by measure, so that sufficiency matched need.
comments.comment: For the saints are permitted, even in this world, to possess what sustains life, as much as would suffice them for the necessary needs of the body. ‘For if we have food and clothing,’ it says, ‘with these we shall be content’ (1 Timothy 6:8). And anything beyond this is not without harm. So small towns and houses, with the fields around them, were assigned to the holy ministers, and these too by measure. For God judged it right this way: he neither indulged them with more than they needed or with luxury, nor pressed them without measure by too tight a limit; but he wisely took away extreme want and removed what causes distress. For he matched sufficiency to need.
comments.selected_reason: Explains why the Levites' towns and lands are of limited size.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 13

comments.capsule: The cities of refuge were entrusted to the Levites, a type of the churches' care for prisoners.
comments.comment: He commands that the cities of refuge be entrusted to the Levites, placing in the care of the priests a class of people who had suffered most and who needed the greatest possible help. Here, I think, the churches have a type: to care for prisoners. For ‘Remember,’ it says, ‘those in bonds, as bound with them, and those who are ill-treated, as being yourselves also in the body’ (Hebrews 13:3)
comments.selected_reason: Explains why the cities of refuge are given to the Levites.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 13

comments.capsule: Those caught in sins are as murderers of their own soul against their will, held as in a city of refuge until Christ the great priest died and released them.
comments.comment: It is not unpersuasive, O Palladius, to think somehow that those caught in the sins are as somehow murderers of their own soul, and have slipped into this misery not willingly, but somehow forced into stepping-beyond, and into striking against God, because the understanding of the human lies upon the evil things from youth, and because of the law that tyrannized in the members of the flesh of the untamed love of pleasure. Therefore the wretched soul of the human is fined with the flight from world and body, and having sat as into some city of refuge-flight in the recesses of death, was continuing through long times, and was released scarcely when Christ the great priest died, who having endured the death for all, has gone down into Hades, and opened gates for those below, and was releasing from bonds, ‘saying to those in bonds, Come out, and to those in the darkness, Be uncovered.’ (Genesis 8:21)
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 8
